title: Interpreter for Nondeterministic Machines
statement: For every effective code system $c$ for two-work-tape nondeterministic binary machines, there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $Q$, a deterministic binary machine $R$ with $K$ work tapes, a work-tape index $j$, and states $\mathrm{entry},\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\in Q$ with $\mathrm{accept}\ne\mathrm{reject}$ such that the following holds. For every binary code $\alpha$, there is a constant $C$ such that for every binary input $x$, time bound $t$, and choice string $s$ with $t\le |s|$, let $z=\langle\langle\operatorname{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, let $N$ be the machine decoded from $\alpha$, and let $e$ be the configuration obtained by running $N$ on $x$ for the first $t$ choices in $s$. Starting $R$ on input $z$ in state $\mathrm{entry}$, with tape $j$ containing $s$ and all other work tapes blank, there is a time $T$ with $T\le C(t+1)$ at which $R$ is in state $\mathrm{accept}$ if and only if $e$ is halted with output $[1]$, and otherwise is in state $\mathrm{reject}$; neither state occurs at any earlier time. Moreover, for every $t'\le t$ such that the run of $N$ using the first $t'$ choices of $s$ is halted, $T\le C(t'+|x|+|\operatorname{bits}(t)|+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective code system for two-work-tape nondeterministic binary machines
$Q$ is finite and has decidable equality
$R$ is a deterministic binary machine with $K$ work tapes
$j$ is a work-tape index and entry, accept, reject are states in $Q$
$x$ is any binary input, $t$ any natural number, and $s$ any binary string with $t\le |s|
replaced:
For every effective code for a nondeterministic binary machine, there are a natural
number $K$, a finite state type $Q$, a deterministic $K$-work-tape machine $R$ over the
binary alphabet, a tape index $j$, and states
$\mathrm{entry},\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\in Q$ with
$\mathrm{accept}\ne\mathrm{reject}$, having the following property. For each binary
string $\alpha$, there is a constant $C$ such that for every binary input $x$, time
bound $t$, and choice string $s$ with $t\le |s|$, set
$z=\langle\langle\operatorname{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, let $N$ be the machine
decoded from $\alpha$, initialize $R$ in state $\mathrm{entry}$ on input $z$ with tape
$j$ containing $s$ and all other work tapes blank, and let $e$ be the result of running
$N$ for $t$ steps using the first $t$ bits of $s$ as choices. There is a time $T\le
C(t+1)$ at which $R$ enters $\mathrm{accept}$ exactly when $e$ has halted with output
$[1]$, and enters $\mathrm{reject}$ otherwise; neither decision state occurs earlier.
Moreover, whenever any prefix of length $t'\le t$ makes $N$ halt, $T\le
C(t'+|x|+|\operatorname{bits}(t)|+1)$.
